Subject: VAT on Apr invoice – mixed supply / request for credit and reissue

Hi Monica / Vanessa,

Hope you’re both well. We reviewed the April invoice (attached) and noticed VAT was charged at 20% on the entire amount. Our company is VAT‑registered in Ireland (VAT: IE1234567E) and most of our subscription usage is B2B SaaS consumed by EU customers — that should generally be subject to reverse‑charge, not charged by Redwood. There are a couple of UK‑facing professional services line items where VAT treatment may differ.

Can you:
- Confirm why VAT was applied across the board;
- Validate our VAT ID (attached certificate) and, if valid, issue a credit for the VAT portion and reissue the invoice reflecting reverse‑charge for the SaaS lines and VAT where applicable for services;
- Provide a proposed proration method if any lines need split treatment.

Attachments: [Attachment: invoice_20270401_ZM-987.pdf (PDF)], [Attachment: vat_certificate_zenmarket_2027.pdf (PDF)].

We need this clarified for our accounts payable cutoffs — target resolution by end of next week if possible.

Thanks,
Ravi

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>

Date: 2027-04-23T10:02:00Z
Subject: Re: VAT on Apr invoice – mixed supply / request for credit and reissue

Hi Ravi — thanks for flagging and for the VAT certificate. We’ll take this through our billing verification and tax routing process. Summary of next steps from our side:

1) VAT ID validation — we’ll run the IE1234567E through VIES and our internal verification. If it validates, SaaS (platform/subscription) lines for B2B customers within the EU are eligible for reverse‑charge.

2) Line‑by‑line classification — we need to confirm which invoice lines are: (a) platform subscription (SaaS), (b) implementation / professional services, (c) marketplace fees (if any). For (a) we expect reverse‑charge once VAT ID is confirmed; for (b) treatment depends on the place of supply — if services are performed in the UK we may need to apply UK VAT.

3) Provisional credit — to avoid disrupting your AP schedule, we can issue a provisional credit equal to the VAT amount on currently charged SaaS lines while we validate. Once validated we’ll either: issue a final credit + reissued invoice (reverse‑charge) or confirm VAT due on specific service lines and provide an adjusted invoice.

Suggested proration approach: allocate the invoice amount by service category. If you cannot provide a pre‑split, we propose a usage‑backed proration using the April usage report (example: 62% SaaS EU usage, 38% professional/UK usage). That will be the basis for the provisional credit calculation.

Can you confirm:
- the registered billing address for the VAT ID (required for VIES follow‑up), and
- whether the April usage report is acceptable for proration.

I’m looping in Karthik to confirm the credit amount and Vanessa for account acceptance. We’ll aim to get the provisional credit posted within 3 business days after you confirm the address.

Best,
Monica Patel
Billing Operations Specialist
Redwood Inference

Monica / Vanessa — quick internal note on proration and credit amount. I pulled April usage from our billing metrics (link below) and ran a quick split:

- SaaS platform tokens (EU B2B consumption): 60%
- Implementation / UK professional services: 30%
- Marketplace/integrations/other taxable items: 10%

If we apply that split to the invoice base (excluding previously charged VAT), and assume your VAT registration validates, the provisional credit for VAT charged on SaaS lines would be: 0.60 x (VAT portion on invoice). Example calculation attached.

I’m comfortable approving a provisional credit up to that amount pending VIES confirmation. Also note: if VIES returns a transient failure, we will request the VAT certificate scan (you already attached) and perform manual validation — that can add 1–2 business days.
